label: Integrated MBSE enables verification of the impact of design decisions on mission requirements throughout the entire mission, beyond standalone STK/MATLAB analysis practice.

linked_evidence_quotes: In the current practice of satellite design, tools such as STK and MATLAB are used to analyze mission performance. However, there is no readily available capability that enables verifying the impact of design decisions on mission requirements throughout the entire mission. The integrated model demonstrates how to accomplish this by performing mission simulations using MBSE models.

source_record.claim_text: Integrated MBSE enables verification of the impact of design decisions on mission requirements throughout the entire mission, beyond standalone STK/MATLAB analysis practice.
source_record.linked_artifact_or_process: SysML satisfy relationships from requirements to Vehicle properties calculated by mission simulation; RAX requirements verification diagram.
source_record.metric_detail: Minimum energy limit, max battery/data capacity, minimum downloaded data per day.
source_record.observed_effect: Requirements were checked using simulation outputs during solar-panel, battery, orbit, and ground-station trade studies.
source_record.threats_alternative_explanations: The comparator is described qualitatively rather than tested; requirement checks are limited to modeled energy/data requirements.

label: Solar-panel area trade study supports EPS design decision-making by showing nominal and half-size panels satisfy the energy requirement while quarter-size panels are too small.

linked_evidence_quotes: When the solar panel area was reduced further, to a quarter of the nominal, the energy level went below the required minimum at the end of the simulation... The results clearly show that the quarter size solar panel is too small for the mission.

source_record.claim_text: Solar-panel area trade study supports EPS design decision-making by showing nominal and half-size panels satisfy the energy requirement while quarter-size panels are too small.
source_record.linked_artifact_or_process: PowerCollection and UpdateEnergy parametric analyses; solar-panel area design instances; energy lower-bound requirement.
source_record.metric_detail: On-board energy level versus 92,000 J minimum bound and 115,000 J max battery capacity.
source_record.observed_effect: Quarter-size solar panel falls below the required minimum by the end of the simulation; half-size and nominal remain within bounds.
source_record.threats_alternative_explanations: Results depend on simplified power/mission assumptions and a prototype RAX model not intended to be accurate to the real satellite.

label: A requirements management model tool can use RMM to automate missing-link checks and support accurate linkage of requirements, test cases, and defects.

linked_evidence_quotes: A Requirements Mapping Matrix (RMM) is best used by a requirement management model tool which can automate the process of checking for missing links [12].

The focus of any testing engagement is, and should be maximum test coverage. By coverage, it simply means that there is a need to test everything there is to be tested. label: The custom MBSE tradespace model supports objective architecture selection and optimization of the BOREALIS baseline configuration.

linked_evidence_quotes: Concept 10 emerges as a standout, positioned prominently on the Pareto front.
Ultimately, the chosen baseline configuration aligns with Concept 10, which balances mission performance with feasibility

Initially, the preferred configuration was Concept 8, featuring a high-thrust monopropellant system. However, as we examined the performance variables in the model, particularly the E_prop parameter (transfer time x mass system), we identified it as the key one that needed to be optimized.
After incorporating it into the model and creating Concept 10, the results demonstrated a clear performance improvement, confirming that this alternative architecture was superior.
To benchmark and validate the BOREALIS CubeSat design decisions, several existing 6U CubeSat missions were integrated into the model as reference architectures.

source_record.claim_text: The custom MBSE tradespace model supports objective architecture selection and optimization of the BOREALIS baseline configuration.
source_record.linked_artifact_or_process: AD matrix, MAU/cost functions, utility-vs-cost tradespace, Pareto front, Concept 10 baseline selection.
source_record.observed_effect: Concept 10 selected as baseline; paper states it balances performance, cost, robustness, and feasibility and improves on initial Concept 8 preference.
source_record.threats_alternative_explanations: Weights are subjective; reference missions benchmark architectures but do not validate MBSE process value; no independent review or physical test is reported.

label: Monte Carlo and sensitivity analyses make the architecture decision robust against uncertainty and subjective weight variation.

linked_evidence_quotes: Concept 10 maintains its relative position as a robust and cost-effective solution, with minimal variability in both utility and cost with respect to the other concepts.
Monte Carlo simulations were performed with 1000 iterations, ensuring statistical significance in capturing the distribution of possible outcomes.
A 95% confidence level was set for the Monte Carlo analysis.

The sensitivity analysis confirms that even varying in a range of $ + / - 30\% $ , the subjective part of the model (weights), no significant changes come out of it. In particular, all the utilities stay in the range of $ + / - 8\% $

source_record.claim_text: Monte Carlo and sensitivity analyses make the architecture decision robust against uncertainty and subjective weight variation.
source_record.linked_artifact_or_process: Monte Carlo uncertainty modeling, utility/cost error bars, sensitivity analyses by AD and concept.
source_record.observed_effect: 1000 Monte Carlo iterations at 95% confidence; all utilities remained within about +/-8% under +/-30% weight changes; Concept 10 retained a robust position.
source_record.threats_alternative_explanations: Robustness is internal to the model assumptions and distributions; it does not demonstrate hardware reliability or mission reliability.

label: The workflow is reusable/adaptable for other CubeSat missions of the same or similar class.

linked_evidence_quotes: Emphasis will be given to the model built for the tradeoff analysis, explaining how it was built and used and providing the reader with all the elements to possibly reuse it for another mission design of the same satellite class.

In this paragraph, the system engineering (SE) process used to develop the BOREALIS 6U bus is presented. It is a systematic approach that can be reused on other missions with the same or similar CubeSat class by adapting the tools that will be presented.

In the context of the BOREALIS mission, MBSE has been integral to aligning complex biological and engineering requirements within the constraints of a CubeSat platform. In the first stage of the mission, a satellite model to evaluate the performance of its different configurations has been developed
The multiple mission concepts were evaluated using Multi-Attribute Utility (MAU) and cost functions to assess their performance and expense.
In this Appendix, the input data to the model to evaluate the BOREALIS mission concepts are reported as referenced in Section 4.3.

label: The structured workflow improves traceability and repeatability from requirements and constraints to architectural decisions and concepts.

linked_evidence_quotes: Unlike traditional document-centric approaches, MBSE employs a model-driven framework to manage requirements, design, analysis, and validation within a centralized environment, which greatly enhances collaboration and traceability across multidisciplinary teams.

The structured workflow we present, from defining architectural decisions (ADs) based on mission constraints, brainstorming viable subsystem options, generating feasible mission concepts, to finally evaluating them through a quantitative framework, ensures traceability and repeatability, making the methodology reusable for future CubeSat missions.
In Figure 3, a summary of the SE process is reported, including the specific deliverables that we chose to manage the mission in accordance with ASI.

Mainly, a Scientific Requirement Document (DEL09) delivered by the biology part of the team presents the main scientific objectives, a Mission Requirement Document (DEL08) collects the high-level and system requirement, and a System Requirement Document (DEL03) deals with the subsystem specifications.

label: Model sharing between MBSE and MDE reuses early ADCS models for onboard software development and allows engineers to focus more on models than programming.

linked_evidence_quotes: From the case study of DelFFi, it can be observed that the key of both MBSE and MDE-based onboard software development is the model. Therefore a bridge between MBSE and onboard software development can be built up through model sharing.

In this step, the ADCS models that have been developed as Simulink blocks for early stage phases and verified using executable SysML are translated automatically to hardware-independent C codes, which are then integrated with low layers of ADCS onboard software to perform Hardware-in-loop simulations.

Using this three-step approach, The ADCS models developed earlier can be re-used, and the engineers can focus more on developing the models rather than programming. A second benefit is the increase in quality of the codes since the consistency of the simulation models and the onboard software is structurally assured.
